headline: On November 8, 2011: Asteroid 2005 YU55 passes Earth
captionCards: 324,600 km from Earth — closest approach since 1976
Over 99% of PHOs pose no threat in the next 100 years
instagramCaption:
Asteroid 2005 YU55 zoomed past Earth.

It came within 0.85 lunar distances—about 324,600 km—making it the closest known approach by an asteroid of its brightness since 1976. The space rock, over 140 meters wide, is classified as a potentially hazardous object due to its size and orbit. Despite its close pass, no impact threat was posed. 

Its flyby highlighted how even distant asteroids can pose future risks if their orbits shift over time.
